# Statement of Applicability — PaketPort Group

The Statement of Applicability lists every control of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, whether it is applicable, why it is included or excluded, how far it is implemented, which approved documents implement it, which risks of the risk register it treats and who owns it (clause 6.1.3 d). It is generated from the control implementation guides under `isms/controls/`, the document set and the risk register; change those sources, not this file.

**Scope.** Group-level statement covering all in-scope entities (PaketPort AT, PaketPort DE, PaketPort CZ). Entity-specific statements with local applicability decisions are generated alongside this file under `soa/`.

**Standard.** ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A. Control titles only; descriptive text is original. Controls introduced with the 2022 revision are marked with *(new)*.

| [A.7.9](../isms/controls/7-physical/A.7.9.md) | Security of assets off-premises | Yes | Technician laptops, tablets, tools, spare parts and locker units are outside PaketPort premises every day; loss or theft of a tablet with maintenance access or a controller with keys is a direct risk (supports R-001 and R-004). | implemented | [POL-PHY](../isms/policies/POL-PHY-physical-and-environmental-security-policy/README.md) | — | Facilities & Physical Security Lead | 3 item(s) |
| [A.7.10](../isms/controls/7-physical/A.7.10.md) | Storage media | Yes | Removable media and the storage inside lockers and controllers carry keys, buffered transactions and backups; encryption, registration and disposal rules prevent leakage (supports R-001 and R-009). | implemented | [POL-CLS](../isms/policies/POL-CLS-asset-management-and-information-classification-policy/README.md) | — | IT Operations Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.7.11](../isms/controls/7-physical/A.7.11.md) | Supporting utilities | Yes | Power and connectivity failures at the head office, the SOC or a locker site interrupt the service; uninterruptible power and safe locker behaviour on power loss protect availability (supports R-003 and R-011). | implemented | [POL-PHY](../isms/policies/POL-PHY-physical-and-environmental-security-policy/README.md) | — | Facilities & Physical Security Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.7.12](../isms/controls/7-physical/A.7.12.md) | Cabling security | Yes | Exposed cabling at locker sites and in offices invites tapping and disruption; protected conduits and treating the locker uplink as untrusted limit the impact. | implemented | [POL-PHY](../isms/policies/POL-PHY-physical-and-environmental-security-policy/README.md) | — | Facilities & Physical Security Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.7.13](../isms/controls/7-physical/A.7.13.md) | Equipment maintenance | Yes | Maintenance is when equipment is opened and technicians — including subcontractors — have their hands on controllers; authorised, recorded maintenance keeps integrity and evidence (supports R-001). | implemented | [POL-PHY](../isms/policies/POL-PHY-physical-and-environmental-security-policy/README.md) | — | Facilities & Physical Security Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.7.14](../isms/controls/7-physical/A.7.14.md) | Secure disposal or re-use of equipment | Yes | Decommissioned lockers, controllers, laptops and media leave PaketPort's control; wiping, certificate revocation and destruction certificates prevent data and key leakage (supports R-001 and R-009). | implemented | [POL-PHY](../isms/policies/POL-PHY-physical-and-environmental-security-policy/README.md) | — | Facilities & Physical Security Lead | 2 item(s) |

| [A.8.6](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.6.md) | Capacity management | Yes | Treats R-011: the API must absorb peaks and attacks, and fleet-wide firmware roll-outs must not starve the management plane; capacity planning keeps the service available. | [A.8.7](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.7.md) | Protection against malware | Yes | Endpoints, servers and the mail gateway are exposed to malware daily, and ransomware in production would threaten the service; the insurer requires endpoint protection (LEG-08); NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g). | implemented | [POL-VULN](../isms/policies/POL-VULN-vulnerability-configuration-management-policy/README.md) | — | Security Engineer | 3 item(s) |

Partially implemented: export alerts and USB blocking are live, outbound content inspection is being tuned. | partially implemented | [POL-CLS](../isms/policies/POL-CLS-asset-management-and-information-classification-policy/README.md) | — | Security Engineer | 2 item(s) |

| [A.8.17](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.17.md) | Clock synchronization | Yes | Treats R-008: correlating events across lockers, backend and identity provider during an investigation requires synchronised clocks, and timelines reported to authorities must be accurate. | implemented | [POL-LOG](../isms/policies/POL-LOG-logging-and-monitoring-policy/README.md) | R-008 | Head of Platform & SRE | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.18](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.18.md) | Use of privileged utility programs | Yes | Treats R-010: database consoles, fleet administration tools and system utilities can bypass application controls; restricting them to named roles through the bastion with session recording keeps them accountable. | implemented | [POL-ACC](../isms/policies/POL-ACC-access-control-policy/README.md) | R-010 | Head of Platform & SRE | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.19](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.19.md) | Installation of software on operational systems | Yes | Treats R-007: unapproved or unsupported software on servers, lockers and endpoints is unpatched software; controlled installation keeps the estate known and patchable (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g)). | implemented | [POL-AUP](../isms/policies/POL-AUP-acceptable-use-policy/README.md), [POL-VULN](../isms/policies/POL-VULN-vulnerability-configuration-management-policy/README.md) | R-007 | IT Operations Lead | 3 item(s) |
| [A.8.20](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.20.md) | Networks security | Yes | Treats R-011 and supports R-001 and R-004: the APIs face the internet and the lockers connect over untrusted networks; firewalls, denial-of-service protection, authenticated remote access and mutual TLS are the backbone (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j)). | implemented | [POL-NET](../isms/policies/POL-NET-network-and-communications-security-policy/README.md) | R-011 | Head of Platform & SRE | 3 item(s) |
| [A.8.21](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.21.md) | Security of network services | Yes | Treats R-011: connectivity, cellular data and content-delivery services are bought in; their security features and service levels must be specified and monitored (LEG-05 carrier API commitments, IP-02). | implemented | [POL-NET](../isms/policies/POL-NET-network-and-communications-security-policy/README.md) | R-011 | Head of Platform & SRE | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.22](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.22.md) | Segregation of networks | Yes | Production, the management plane, corporate IT, the lab and the untrusted locker estate must not share trust; segregation limits the blast radius of a compromised locker, laptop or test unit (supports R-001 and R-004; NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j)). | implemented | [POL-NET](../isms/policies/POL-NET-network-and-communications-security-policy/README.md) | — | Head of Platform & SRE | 3 item(s) |
| [A.8.23](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.23.md) | Web filtering *(new)* | Yes | Treats R-005: malicious and phishing sites deliver credential theft and malware; filtering on all managed devices, including field laptops, blocks them early (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g)). | [A.8.24](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.24.md) | Use of cryptography | Yes | Treats R-001 and R-009: mutual TLS and signed firmware protect the lockers, encryption at rest and in transit protects consumer data; NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h) and the Cyber Resilience Act require managed cryptography. | implemented | [POL-CRYP](../isms/policies/POL-CRYP-cryptography-policy/README.md), [STD-CRYPTO](../isms/standards/STD-CRYPTO-cryptographic-algorithms-and-key-lengths-standard/README.md) | R-001, R-009 | Head of Platform & SRE | 4 item(s) |
| [A.8.25](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.25.md) | Secure development life cycle | Yes | Treats R-009: security built into the requirements, design, coding, testing and release of firmware, backend and app; required for the locker product by the Cyber Resilience Act (LEG-03) and by NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e). | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | R-009 | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.26](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.26.md) | Application security requirements | Yes | Treats R-009: without explicit requirements for authentication, authorisation, input validation, cryptography and logging, features ship insecure; the locker product's essential requirements under the Cyber Resilience Act must be documented. | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | R-009 | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.27](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.27.md) | Secure system architecture and engineering principles | Yes | Defence in depth, least privilege, fail-secure lockers and no implicit trust between locker, backend and app are what keep a single flaw from becoming a fleet-wide compromise (supports R-001 and R-009). | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | — | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.28](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.28.md) | Secure coding *(new)* | Yes | Treats R-009: injection, memory errors in firmware and leaked secrets are coding defects; a coding standard with automated checks and four-eyes review prevents them (LEG-03; NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e)). | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | R-009 | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.29](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.29.md) | Security testing in development and acceptance | Yes | Treats R-009: static and dynamic testing, hardware-in-the-loop firmware tests and annual penetration tests find what reviews miss before attackers do. | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | R-009 | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.30](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.30.md) | Outsourced development | Yes | Treats R-006: code written by an external developer enters PaketPort's products; contracts, access limits, testing before acceptance and no production data keep it to the same standard (LEG-03 for product components; NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d)). | implemented | [POL-SUP](../isms/policies/POL-SUP-supplier-cloud-security-policy/README.md) | R-006 | Head of Procurement | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.31](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.31.md) | Separation of development, test and production environments | Yes | Separate development, test, staging and production with separate credentials and no production data stop a test mistake or a compromised developer account from reaching the fleet or consumer data (supports R-009 and R-004). | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | — | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.32](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.32.md) | Change management | Yes | Uncontrolled changes to production, the fleet or the ISMS cause outages and security gaps; typed changes with approval, testing, rollback and staged firmware roll-outs keep change safe (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e); clause 6.3). | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | — | Software Engineering Lead | 3 item(s) |
| [A.8.33](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.33.md) | Test information | Yes | Real consumer data in test systems would extend the breach surface to every developer laptop and lab unit (supports R-009); masked or synthetic test data removes it. | implemented | [POL-SDLC](../isms/policies/POL-SDLC-secure-development-and-change-management-policy/README.md) | — | Software Engineering Lead | 2 item(s) |
| [A.8.34](../isms/controls/8-technological/A.8.34.md) | Protection of information systems during audit testing | Yes | Audits and penetration tests touch production and the fleet; read-only access, approved windows and confidential handling of audit data prevent the assurance activity from causing an incident. | implemented | [PROC-AUDIT](../isms/procedures/PROC-AUDIT-internal-audit-procedure/README.md) | — | Internal Audit Lead | 2 item(s) |

## Approval

Maintained by the Information Security Officer / ISMS Manager; approved by the Managing Director as part of the risk treatment plan (PROC-RISK). Approval and every subsequent change are recorded in version control through the pull-request history of the control guides.
